title: Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt
capsule: The Seventeenth Dynasty ruled Upper Egypt from Thebes during the late Second Intermediate Period, coexisting with the Hyksos Fifteenth Dynasty in the Delta and the Kushite kingdom to the south, from approximately 1580 to 1550 BCE. The dynasty's last rulers, Seqenenre Tao and Kamose, launched the wars of reunification against the Hyksos: Seqenenre Tao died violently in battle (his mummy shows multiple fatal head wounds), and Kamose advanced as far north as the outskirts of Avaris before his premature death. Ahmose I, founder of the Eighteenth Dynasty, completed the expulsion of the Hyksos around 1550 BCE, reunifying Egypt and inaugurating the New Kingdom. The Seventeenth Dynasty's rulers left behind some of Egypt's finest Middle Egyptian literary and administrative texts.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Seventeenth Dynasty is moderately attested from royal inscriptions and stelae, but its northern boundary with Hyksos-controlled Egypt fluctuated and is imprecisely known from the surviving record.
